environment.description: ECS Fargate task in private subnet with identical application code. The internal admin API is fronted by an AWS ALB configured with mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication on the HTTPS:443 listener. The listener's MutualAuthentication block specifies Mode=verify with a TrustStore ARN pointing to an ACM PCA-issued intermediate CA. The order-consumer task's HTTP client is configured WITHOUT a client certificate keystore (the Java HttpClient instantiation uses default SSL context with no KeyManagerFactory). The ALB's listener rule requires valid client certificate presentation before forwarding ANY request to the admin-api target group. Additionally, the ALB access logs show that connections without valid client certs receive immediate TLS handshake failures (error_reason=ClientCertRequired). The trust store only contains certificates issued by the internal PKI root 'arn:aws:acm-pca:us-east-1:123456789:certificate-authority/ca-abc123' and the order-consumer service was deployed from a container image that does not bundle any client certificate material.

config.admin_api_alb: Internal ALB, HTTPS:443 listener, MutualAuthentication Mode=verify, TrustStoreArn=arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:123456789:truststore/internal-pki-ts/ts-0abc123def
config.alb_listener_rule: Default action: forward to admin-api-tg, condition: ALL requests must pass mTLS verification
config.order_consumer_ssl_context: Default JVM SSLContext, no client certificate configured, no PKCS12 keystore mounted
config.sqs_policy: Allow SendMessage from any authenticated AWS principal in account
config.admin_api_backend: Interpolates action field into shell command without additional sanitization
config.tls_enforcement: ALB drops connections at TLS layer if no valid client cert presented; HTTP request never reaches target group
